name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
description: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, spoken dialogue, multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and multimodal image-audio understanding.
creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed by extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from source datasets and organizing them into listening, speaking, and viewing subsets. The authors collected source data from 23 audio understanding datasets for listening, 22 datasets plus RoleBench for speaking, and MMMU for viewing; Appendix E lists 47 source datasets total. They converted collected text instructions into audio, selected 100 distinct roles and collected three representative audio clips per role for role-play, and curated the benchmark through deduplication, validation, categorization, and balanced sampling, resulting in 10,497 high-quality samples.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Incomplete or unsuitable instances were excluded, including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, missing or broken audio or images, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers. Approximately 10% of candidates were discarded at this stage.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data were drawn from 47 source datasets spanning audio, speech, music, dialogue, text, and images. Listening used 23 audio understanding datasets; speaking used RoleBench plus 22 other datasets including 11 text datasets and 11 audio datasets; viewing used MMMU. The benchmark also reused 300 role audio clips from the role-play task as prompt audio for speech synthesis.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Collected text instructions were converted into audio. For speech synthesis, image reference tokens were replaced with descriptive phrases, text was rewritten to be more suitable for TTS, and multiple-choice options were rephrased for readability. The authors de-duplicated content using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance, manually reviewed suspected duplicates, mapped examples to 13 task categories based primarily on source metadata, and applied balanced sampling to equalize category representation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Texts were preprocessed before synthesis by replacing special image tokens with descriptive phrases, rewriting text with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct so numbers and mathematical expressions would be read accurately, and rephrasing multiple-choice options for readability. During curation, the authors filtered out incomplete or inappropriate items, including corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and incorrect answers.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark uses reference answers and labels inherited or adapted from source datasets, and includes manual curation decisions. For validation, curators reviewed each candidate item in a web-based tool and assigned a Good or Bad verdict with optional notes after checking media integrity, task well-posedness, and answer validity. For evaluation of model outputs, automated judges used task-specific prompts with gpt-oss-20b for content judgments, emotion2vec for emotion probabilities, UTMOS for speech quality, Whisper-Large-v3 for transcription, and Wespeaker for speaker similarity in role-play.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Suspected duplicates were manually reviewed and removed. The curation tool exported an audit log with item IDs, curator decisions, and timestamps. For evaluation validation, the authors randomly sampled 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B responses from each of the 13 tasks, resulting in 1,050 examples, and had them independently evaluated by human judges. They report strong agreement between automated and human evaluation, with overall Pearson correlation 0.92 and agreement rate 96.1%.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, UTMOS Strong, Whisper-Large-v3, gpt-oss-20b, emotion2vec, Wespeaker
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that they will release both the dataset and evaluation code publicly. They also state they will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes speaker voices for role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation. It also includes user emotions with seven emotion categories. The paper notes five Chinese roles in the role-play task, while all other prompts and evaluations are in English.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses that the benchmark can help develop next-generation multimodal AI assistants and track progress toward expert AI assistants. It also highlights risks related to voice imitation, including identity spoofing, harassment, fraud, impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics. The authors propose safeguards including documented consent, consent gating, watermarking or traceability of synthetic audio, safety cards, and governance for auditing and removal.
rai:dataBiases: The authors state that the benchmark may carry biases from its source data and design choices. Questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, such as existing datasets and rewritten instructions, which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments. They note that the role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts, which may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. They also note that automated measures and GPT-based scoring may introduce noise and bias and may favor certain phrasings or overlook nuanced errors.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may be limited in diversity despite its size; although it includes five Chinese roles in the role-play task, all other prompts and evaluations are in English, limiting generalization to more diverse linguistic settings. The benchmark may carry biases from academic or synthetic source data and fixed role prompts. Task coverage is incomplete, excluding video-audio integration, continuous audio-visual streaming, latency, partial utterances, barge-in, and error recovery. The evaluation is offline and static, and automated GPT-based scoring may introduce noise and bias.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating voice assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing, and for facilitating future research on multimodal AI assistants. The paper explicitly states it is not supposed to be used for training models for cheating. The authors intend researchers to use it to better evaluate voice assistants. They also prohibit training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent and require downstream users to implement consent gating and watermarking or traceability of synthetic audio.
